target_customer: Shippers, railroads, transloaders, carriers, plants and merchants running rail and bulk operations
problem: Rail, transload and bulk work runs on spreadsheets, paper tickets, phone calls and disconnected legacy systems, so data is entered twice and inventory is hard to see.
business_model: B2B SaaS across operations, tracking and finance modules; says no onboarding fee and no billing until go-live
product_category: AI-native software for rail and bulk operations

founders.name: Warren Wijaya Wang
founders.background_notes: Led product at Milk Moovement; emigrated from Indonesia in 2016 per Startland News

founders.name: Cole Robertson
previous_startups: SaaS consulting business reaching 300K in just over a year per YC page
founders.background_notes: Engineer 3 at Tropic from seed to Series B per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Full operations suite plus computer vision bulk scanning and AI automation over legacy systems is broad but standard engineering for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Becoming the system of record for railcars, inventory and billing in small operators creates switching costs; the market is niche and incumbents like IntelliTrans exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent transload tools target similar users; no evidence they copied the AI approach or bought Rebulk.

market_need_then: Operators run on paper and spreadsheets; the company's customers include Venezia Transport, Usher Transport and TransloadX, and a Cargill pilot is reported by Startland News.

branding.name_origin: Chief of staff Kenneth Bautista first suggested the name; founder Warren Wang says it feels like the right name for the future they want to build (Startland News)

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical: Your operation shouldn't run on spreadsheets

branding.brand_signature: Your operation shouldn't run on spreadsheets

rebrands.why: Company moved from video transcription to AI for tracking bulk materials and later rail and bulk operations; Startland News reports the rename around 2026-03-20

branding.community_and_virality: Featured in Bulk Transporter, the BulkLoads Podcast and The Waterways Journal per its own site; local coverage by Startland News.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive name that fits the bulk focus, trade press and local news, though the rebrand is recent and a niche audience.

pivots.to: Computer vision for measuring bulk inventory
pivots.why: Not stated in opened sources; Startland News describes the shift

pivots.from: Bulk inventory scanning with drones and cameras
pivots.to: Broader AI native software for rail, transload and bulk operations
pivots.why: Not stated; YC launch post described scanning while the YC page now describes the full suite

outcome_analysis: Rebulk moved from transcription to bulk inventory scanning and then to a full rail and bulk operations suite, with paying customers, a Cargill pilot and a 1.2M pre-seed from Kansas City investors. Founders with supply chain experience help, but it is tiny, in a niche market with older transload software vendors, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Pre-seed amount comes from Startland News (which links its March 2025 story) and a yespress.io profile lists 1.33M total; investors named (KCRise Fund, Abstraction Capital, Flyover Capital, Redbud VC, EquipmentShare) are not tied to this round by the source so the list is empty. Round date is from the referenced story title month. Founder education not listed. No dated competitor sources near the batch; only generic transload vendor listings found.
